title: measure_packet_motion.py: ZeroDivisionError when the after-strip has no moving frames
evidence: print(f"mean jump when moving: BEFORE={sum(b_steps)/len(b_steps):.1f}px  AFTER={sum(a_steps)/len(a_steps):.1f}px")
detail: The mean line is guarded only by `if b_steps:`. If the after dir has zero moving frames (window fully post-arrival, packet off-frame), len(a_steps)==0 and the tool crashes. Reproduced: after-dir of all-holds frames → ZeroDivisionError.
recommended_fix: Guard the AFTER mean on a_steps too: print BEFORE only, or `AFTER=n/a` when a_steps is empty.

title: measure_packet_motion.py: zip(before, after) silently truncates on frame-count mismatch
evidence:
for (fb, db), (fa, da) in zip(before, after):
        print(f"{fb} | {db:6.1f} | {da:6.1f}")
    b_holds = sum(1 for _, d in before if d < 0.5)
    a_holds = sum(1 for _, d in after if d < 0.5)
detail: Dirs with different frame counts (different end_ms/step_ms) pair positionally and drop the tail silently; the holds/mean stats still use full lengths. Reproduced: before=3/after=4 frames printed a 3-row table with 'AFTER=3/4' — misleading evidence with no warning.
recommended_fix: Compare len(before)/len(after) (and frame-name sequences) before printing; exit 2 on mismatch.

title: measure_packet_motion.py: missing dir or stray non-PNG file crashes with a raw traceback
detail: No existence or format validation: a missing/misspelled dir raises FileNotFoundError; a stray non-PNG entry (e.g. macOS .DS_Store) raises PIL UnidentifiedImageError. Both reproduced. Loud but unhandled input paths in new code.
recommended_fix: Guard os.path.isdir and filter entries to *.png (skip others or fail with a clean message).

title: motion-strip: a 6th arg other than exactly "snapshot" is silently ignored (interp mode runs)
evidence: code := run_motion_strip(rest[0], rest[1], rest[2], rest[3], rest[4], len(rest) == 6 && rest[5] == "snapshot", &cat, &rc)
detail: Any 6th token except the exact string "snapshot" (typo, casing) is accepted and silently selects interpolated mode; only the final stdout line discloses the mode. Unvalidated CLI input path in new code.
recommended_fix: Reject a 6th arg that isn't "snapshot": `if len(rest) == 6 && rest[5] != "snapshot" { usage() }`.

title: render_strip_frame ignores rl.ExportImage's failure and still counts the frame — verb reports success with an empty/partial outdir
evidence:
path := fmt.tprintf("%s/%s-%06dms.png", outdir, demo_name, ms)
	rl.ExportImage(img, strings.clone_to_cstring(path, context.temp_allocator))
	rl.UnloadImage(img)
	frames^ += 1
detail: On a failed write (unwritable outdir, disk full) every export can fail yet `frames` increments and the verb exits 0 printing "N frame(s)". Sibling evidence verbs check the bool (goldens.odin:146 `ok := rl.ExportImage(...)`, map_preview.odin:117, overlay.odin:122, wire_preview.odin:108).
recommended_fix: Bind and check the result like map_preview: `if !rl.ExportImage(img, ...) { fmt.eprintfln("motion-strip: export failed: %s", path); return 2 }`.
